item.title: #3620031: Adopt the three-tier protocol: block Restricted images, warn on Moderate
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +100/−28 · md +88/−18 · yml +10/−8 · json +2/−2
  • Diff: 2469b0d
  • Discussion: #3620031 · 2 contributors · 11 comments
  • Followers: 3
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 2 contributors

Summary

The image safety recipe now has three tiers instead of a binary block. Safe images save silently. Moderate images (partial nudity, suggestive content, mild violence) are accepted, and the uploader sees a warning. Restricted images (full nudity, explicit sexual content, gore, graphic violence, graphic medical imagery) are still blocked with a validation error. An image the model cannot classify is treated as Restricted. Sites that already applied the recipe do not pick this up automatically.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: drupal/ai_validations constraint raised from ^1.3 to ^1.4, which provides the opt-in XSAFE/XWARN/XBLOCK warning tier (#3606131).
  • Config change: Shipped field_validation.rule_set.media_image rule: new title, XSAFE/XWARN/XBLOCK prompt, reworded message, new warningMessage key in the rule data.

Technical details

The rule's prompt in config/field_validation.rule_set.media_image.yml now returns XSAFE, XWARN or XBLOCK in place of XTRUE/XFALSE. The rule title becomes "Block restricted imagery, warn on moderate". The message text now covers only Restricted content, and the new warningMessage key in the rule's data holds the Moderate text. The rule's provider is unchanged, an empty string meaning the site default. recipe.yml and the composer.json description are reworded, and composer.json requires drupal/ai_validations ^1.4.

The warning tier is opt-in in AI Validations and is active only while the warning message is non-empty. The README says that emptying it returns validation to XTRUE/XFALSE, and that the prompt must then be rewritten to match. If only one of the two is changed, uploads are blocked (empty message with the three-token prompt) or no warning is ever shown (message set with the two-token prompt). The README also documents "Adjusting the tiers", for example mapping Moderate to XBLOCK or XSAFE. It states that an XWARN verdict also writes to the ai_validations logger channel, so headless flows such as JSON:API keep an audit trail and are never blocked by a warning.

Upgrade

The recipe creates the rule set with createIfNotExists, so re-applying the new version on a site that already has the media_image rule set changes nothing. Either delete the rule set at Structure → Field Validation and re-apply the recipe, or edit the existing rule by hand:

=== DECISION ===
- If the image is SAFE, respond with: XSAFE
- If the image is MODERATE, respond with: XWARN
- If the image is RESTRICTED, respond with: XBLOCK

=== OUTPUT FORMAT ===
Respond with exactly one token — XSAFE, XWARN, or XBLOCK — and nothing else.

Then fill in the rule's Warning message field. Update drupal/ai_validations to 1.4 or newer.

item.title: #3586825: Forward/Backward-Port: Add automator ID tag and entity_context to chat requests (1.4.x & 2.0.x)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 28 files, +2871/−10 · php +2685/−10 · md +186
  • Diff: cbe279c
  • Discussion: #3586825 · 1 contributor · 16 comments

Summary

Chat requests that AI Automators send to a provider now identify which automator made them. Each request gets an ai_automator:id:{config entity ID} tag and an entity_context metadata array describing the entity and field. Several automators on the same field (for example separate Field Widget Action buttons) previously produced requests with identical tags, so event subscribers could not tell them apart. This was ported to 2.0.x/2.x and backported to 1.4.x after landing on 1.x and 1.5.x (#3586702).

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: On 1.4.x the InputBase request metadata methods (getAllRequestMetadata(), setAllRequestMetadata(), getRequestMetadataValue(), setRequestMetadataValue()) are added, and ProviderProxy seeds pre and post event metadata from the input. Code that rebuilds the automator config array in AutomatorConfigEvent subscribers on 1.4.x must keep the id key.
  • New API: Automator chat requests carry a new ai_automator:id:{automator config entity ID} tag and entity_context request metadata (entity_type, entity_id, uuid, bundle, field_name, automator_id). New protected RuleBase::buildEntityContext() and RuleBase::attachEntityContext() helpers.

Technical details

RuleBase::getTags() now adds ai_automator:id:{id} when the automator config carries a string ID. RuleBase::runRawChatMessage() and the rich-text image description path in RichTextImageDescriptionTrait call the new attachEntityContext() on the final input, after applyGuardrailsToInput(), because that helper can return a clone. buildEntityContext() returns entity_type, entity_id, uuid, bundle, field_name and automator_id. entity_id is NULL for new (unsaved) entities, so presave requests are identified by uuid. The metadata is read with $event->getMetadata('entity_context'). Rules that build their own ChatInput (Chart, VideoToText, LlmVideo*, Field Widget Action refine chat) still send untagged requests, as the added docs state.

On 2.0.x/2.x the automator ID, field name and plugin ID are not stored settings. AiAutomatorEntityModifier::withRuntimeContext() clones each automator type and adds automator_id, field_name and rule to its settings, so nothing leaks into exported config. These runtime settings are set after the stored ones, so a stray stored setting with the same key cannot override them. RunAutomatorAction sets the same three keys, and the tag and metadata read automator_id.

On 1.4.x the ID lives in the id key of the runtime automator config instead. AiAutomatorEntityModifier::entityHasConfig() and RunAutomatorAction set it from the config entity ID, after the plugin_config keys are unprefixed. RuleBase::attachEntityContext() there is guarded with method_exists($input, 'setRequestMetadataValue'). The 1.4.x commit also adds request metadata to InputBase. ProviderProxy seeds the PreGenerateResponseEvent metadata from the input and passes the post event metadata to streamed responses. It also re-applies the input's system prompt to the provider after the pre-generate event, so event subscribers can change it.

Upgrade

Subscribers can target one automator by tag:

public function onPreGenerate(PreGenerateResponseEvent $event): void {
  if (!in_array('ai_automator:id:node.article.field_summary.default', $event->getTags(), TRUE)) {
    return;
  }
  $context = $event->getMetadata('entity_context');
  // $context['entity_id'] is NULL on presave; fall back to uuid or bundle.
}

Custom rules that build their own ChatInput should call $this->attachEntityContext($input, $entity, $automatorConfig); and pass $this->getTags(...) to chat(). On 2.x, code calling a rule outside AiAutomatorEntityModifier or RunAutomatorAction must add automator_id, field_name and rule to the settings itself. On 1.4.x, AutomatorConfigEvent subscribers that rebuild the config array must keep its id key, or the ID tag and automator_id are dropped.

item.title: #3564627: Tool for views exec
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +147/−0 · php +140 · yml +7
  • Discussion: #3564627 · 2 contributors · 7 comments
  • Followers: 3
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 2 contributors

Summary

The merge request adds a tool that runs a View and returns its rendered output, so tool consumers such as AI agents can call a View by machine name, display ID and arguments. It ships as a new Tool - Views module. Access follows the chosen View display's own access rules. The MR was still a draft proposal when summarized, and a comment suggested moving the work to the Tool Belt project.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New tool_views module with a views_execute Tool plugin (Drupal\tool_views\Plugin\tool\Tool\ViewsExecute) taking view_name, display_id and arguments.

Technical details

The MR adds a tool_views module (it depends on tool:tool) containing the ViewsExecute plugin, declared with #[Tool(id: 'views_execute', operation: ToolOperation::Trigger)]. Inputs are view_name (string), display_id (string, default default) and arguments (map, optional). doExecute() loads the View with Views::getView() and calls setDisplay(). It fails with an ExecutableResult::failure() if either the View or the display is missing. Otherwise it calls setArguments(), execute() and render(). A render array result is turned into a string with the renderer service's renderRoot(). An empty result becomes the placeholder [No output returned by view]. The output is a results map with a single output string.

checkAccess() returns forbidden when the View or display does not exist. Otherwise it delegates to $view->display_handler->access($account) and wraps a non-AccessResultInterface result as allowed or forbidden. The .info.yml description mentions tools for creating, modifying and removing views, but only execution is implemented in this diff.

item.title: #3563382: EntityFieldValues tool doesn't return image field metadata (alt, title, width, height)
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +10/−2 · php +10/−2
  • Discussion: #3563382 · 4 contributors · 9 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

The entity_field_values tool now returns more data for entity reference fields that carry extra properties, such as a media entity's image field. Before, you only got the target_id and basic entity info. Now alt, title, width and height come back too. This helps agents and other consumers that need image metadata from the tool's output. The merge request is a proposal and no commit had landed when this was written.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The problem was in getFieldItemValue() in src/Plugin/tool/Tool/EntityFieldValues.php. It returned early on any field with a target_id property, so it only returned target_id and an entity array (id, label, type). In the MR, that branch builds a $result array with the same two keys. It then loops over all field item properties and adds each one that is not computed and is not target_id, keyed by property name, using $property->getValue(). The result is returned afterwards.

The issue's proposed code skipped NULL and empty-string values. After review, the MR includes every non-computed property, empty values too, because no reason to filter them was found. The module maintainer questioned whether a field-type-agnostic approach would be better. He suggested the isset($properties['target_id']) block might be removable, but said that may not be possible. That question was not settled in the thread, and the diff keeps the target_id branch.

item.title: #3553442: [Tools] Create ConfigSet tool
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 1 file, +136/−0 · php +136
  • Discussion: #3553442 · 4 contributors · 8 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

Adds a "Set Configuration" tool that lets a tool caller, such as an MCP client or AI agent, change one value in an existing configuration object. The caller gives a config name (e.g. system.site), a key (e.g. slogan) and a value. The tool returns the old and new values. In the issue, it was tested by asking Claude Desktop over MCP to change the site name and slogan. Near the end of the thread a maintainer proposed moving the issue to the Tool Belt module, since tools are being moved out of Tool API. The MR has not been committed to this project.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New config_set Tool plugin (Drupal\tool_system\Plugin\tool\Tool\ConfigSet) in the tool_system module.

Technical details

The MR adds a single final class, ConfigSet, as a #[Tool] plugin with id config_set. Its inputs are config_name (string), key (string) and value (any). It has one output, updated_config (any).

doExecute() loads the object with ConfigFactoryInterface::getEditable(). If isNew() is true, it returns ExecutableResult::failure() instead of creating a new config object. Otherwise it reads the old value with get($key), then calls set() and save(). It returns a success message plus updated_config containing config_name, key, old_value and new_value. Any \Exception is caught and returned as a failure result. Non-scalar values are JSON-encoded in the message only.

checkAccess() returns AccessResult::allowedIfHasPermission($account, 'administer site configuration'). The tool does not validate the key or value against the config schema in the code shown. The set()/save() call is the only write step.

item.title: #3553440: [Tools] Create ConfigGet tool
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev

  • Changes: 2 files, +128/−0 · php +123 · yml +5
  • Discussion: #3553440 · 5 contributors · 12 comments
  • Followers: 6

Summary

The Tool module's tool_system submodule gets a new "Get Configuration" tool. It lets a caller, such as an AI agent over MCP, read a configuration object from Drupal, either in full or a single key like the site name from system.site. Access needs the new use config_get tool permission. That permission exposes any configuration, so grant it only to trusted roles. The merge request was marked as looking good but had not been committed when this summary was written.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Permission change: New use config_get tool permission in tool_system, which allows reading any configuration.
  • New API: New config_get Tool plugin (ConfigGet) in tool_system for reading configuration objects or single keys.

Technical details

The change adds Drupal\tool_system\Plugin\tool\Tool\ConfigGet, a ToolOperation::Read tool with id config_get. Inputs are config_name (required string) and key (optional string). The single output is config_value of type any. The issue text lists key without saying it is optional, but the MR makes it optional: an empty key returns all data for the object.

doExecute() loads the object through config.factory. It returns ExecutableResult::failure() if isNew() is true, meaning the object does not exist. Otherwise it returns $config->get($key) or $config->get(). A code comment says get() is used instead of getRawData() so that overrides are included. Any \Exception is caught and returned as a failure result. checkAccess() uses AccessResult::allowedIfHasPermission($account, 'use config_get tool'). The permission is defined in the tool_system permissions YAML with the description "Allows users to fetch any configuration from Drupal."

item.title: #3556021: [Tool] Create tools to save/update/delete SDC components
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 10 files, +1271/−0 · php +1256 · yml +15
  • Discussion: #3556021 · 5 contributors · 23 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

This adds a Tool module, tool_sdc, that lets Tool API callers such as AI agents build Single Directory Components (SDC) in a theme or module. The tools list existing components, read component files, write the .component.yml definition, the .twig template and css, js, scss or json files, and delete files. The tools write directly into theme or module directories on the filesystem. For that reason they sit behind two new permissions, and the write permission is marked as restricted. Only grant it on local or development environments. The issue is marked fixed, but no commits had landed when this was summarized. A late comment says the Tool project's tools are moving to the Tool Belt module (see #3557721), so the final home of this code may differ.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Permission change: New read filesystem components permission and a new restricted write filesystem components permission.
  • New API: New tool_sdc submodule in the Tool project with seven tool plugins (list_components, list_component_files, read_component_file, write_sdc_definition, write_sdc_twig, write_sdc_file, delete_component_file) and an SdcToolBase base class.

Technical details

This is based on the MR !57 diff, which is a proposal and not merged code. A new tool_sdc module depends on tool:tool. Its tools are #[Tool] plugins in Drupal\tool_sdc\Plugin\tool\Tool, all extending SdcToolBase. The base class injects module_handler, theme_handler, file_system, plugin.manager.sdc and app.root. It resolves the extension path and builds the path <extension>/components/<component_name>. Write tools call ComponentPluginManager::clearCachedDefinitions() after changing files.

Each tool takes component_name (regex-constrained), extension_type (theme or module) and extension_name. Path safety comes from sanitizeFilePath(), sanitizeFileName(), getComponentDirectory() and validateFilePath(). These reject .. and null bytes and check that the resolved path stays inside the component directory. write_sdc_definition only checks that the YAML parses with Yaml::parse(). It does not check it against the SDC schema. write_sdc_twig checks syntax by tokenizing with the twig service.

File type allowlists: write_sdc_file accepts css, js, scss and json. read_component_file accepts those plus twig, yml and yaml. delete_component_file refuses twig, yml and yaml, so a component itself has to be removed by hand. Access is decided in SdcToolBase::checkAccess(). Tools whose operation is ToolOperation::Read need read filesystem components. All others need write filesystem components, which is declared with restrict access: true. The copy_sdc_file tool from the original proposal was dropped.

Contribution

item.title: #3554737: [Tool] Create Date/Time Formatter tool
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +458/−0 · php +451 · yml +7
  • Discussion: #3554737 · 4 contributors · 8 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 4 contributors

Summary

The Tool project gets a "Format Date/Time" tool that converts a timestamp, a date string or a relative expression such as "+1 day" into a formatted string. You can choose the output format, timezone and language. It can also return a relative time difference instead of an absolute date. It ships in a new tool_utilities submodule for generic utility tools and needs no access check, so anyone can run it. The merge request was marked RTBC after testing, but the diff was still unmerged when this was written.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New date_time_formatter tool plugin (Drupal\tool_utilities\Plugin\tool\Tool\DateTimeFormatter) in a new tool_utilities submodule.

Technical details

The tool is a ToolBase plugin with id date_time_formatter and the Read operation. Its inputs are input_value (required), input_format, output_format (default Y-m-d H:i:s), timezone, locale and relative (default FALSE). It has one output, formatted_date.

Input parsing happens in parseInput(). A numeric value is treated as a Unix timestamp. Otherwise \DateTime::createFromFormat() is used when input_format is given, and new \DateTime() is used when it is not. The timezone value is applied when parsing the string as well as when formatting the output. Any parse failure, including an invalid timezone, returns ExecutableResult::failure().

When relative is set, the tool calls DateFormatterInterface::formatTimeDiffSince(), passing locale as langcode. Otherwise it calls DateFormatterInterface::format(). If output_format matches the ID of a date_format config entity such as short or medium, that entity is used. If not, the string is used as a custom PHP date format. checkAccess() always returns allowed.

The MR also adds a tool_utilities.info.yml. It requires Drupal ^10.3 || ^11 and depends on tool:tool. A unit test, DateTimeFormatterTest, covers timestamp, string, timezone, relative and date format entity inputs. It uses a mocked date.formatter service, so it does not check real timezone or locale output.

Contribution

item.title: #3586618: Drupal tokens in context item text are replaced on the agent path only
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 24 files, +1343/−31 · php +1158/−18 · md +178/−13 · yml +7
  • Diff: c5f438e
  • Discussion: #3586618 · 1 contributor · 22 comments

Summary

Drupal tokens in context item text are no longer replaced when context reaches the AI. Before this change, AI Agents ran token replacement over the whole system prompt, so an item containing [user:mail] sent the email of whoever ran the agent to the AI provider, and [user:uuid] stopped the agent run with an error. The same happened in the List, Load and Get Relevant tool output when a site used them as default information tools. CCC now writes tokens with a space on both sides of the colon, for example [user : mail], on the agent path, the generic chat path, the three tools and the public selection API. Sites that used tokens in item text on purpose must write the real values into the text. Items that document token patterns (for example [node:title] for URL aliases) now show them with spaces, so authors may want to tell the agent to remove the spaces when writing a token into a field. The Context prefix setting is not changed, so [site:name] there is still replaced on the agent path.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Personal data leak: [user:mail] in context item text was replaced by AI Agents with the running user's email and sent to the AI provider. Item text is now neutralized on every path.
  • Config change: Context prefix is still token-replaced on the agent path; Content and Context prefix field help texts now say how tokens are treated.

Technical details

A new @internal service ai_context.token_neutralizer (AiContextTokenNeutralizer) uses Token::scan() and rewrites each match to [type : name], so a later scan no longer matches. It handles every type from Token::getInfo(). It also handles undeclared types that look like token types (for example ECA's [current_user:mail]) when the first part of the name has no whitespace, / or @. Root-level data paths such as [current_user.mail.value] are broken when the part before the first dot is a declared type or current_user. Root-level matches without a colon, such as [2] or [optional], are left alone. It rescans up to three times, because ECA's scan() can hide root-level tokens behind a literal [_eca_root_token:x]. Side effects: items[i:j], some IPv6 forms like [fd12:3456::1], and dotted Markdown links like [node.js](...) also get the spaces.

It is applied in three places. AiContextRenderer neutralizes the assembled text, so the token budget is checked on the neutralized text and tokens spanning fields are caught. AiContextSelector neutralizes the final text after TEXT_RENDERED subscribers run, and the label, purpose and content_snippet in the selected-item data. ListAiContextItems neutralizes its own output, because it does not use the renderer. The renderer and selector constructors take the neutralizer as a new last argument, and the service definitions are updated.

Documented limits: each output is neutralized separately, so deliberately split tokens across joined outputs can still be replaced. Sites that decorate ai_context.selection_factory must return the inner factory text. Sites that replace it must break tokens in their own output. To read item text as written, load the ai_context_item entity.

Upgrade

The output of getRenderedContext(), getResult(), getResultFromSelection(), AiContextSelectionResult::getSelectedItems() and TEXT_RENDERED text now has tokens neutralized, for example [user:mail] becomes [user : mail]. To read item text with its tokens as written, load the context item entity and read its fields. If you replace ai_context.selection_factory, put a space on both sides of the colon of Drupal tokens in the text you return, because ai_context.token_neutralizer is internal. If you decorate it, return the inner factory text and do not add item text from other sources.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 18, 2026
  • Committed: November 2, 2026 (14 days later)

item.title: #3586616: Unpublished context item translations can be delivered to AI prompts
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 13 files, +684/−72 · php +627/−55 · md +53/−17 · json +4
  • Diff: af8ece4
  • Discussion: #3586616 · 1 contributor · 26 comments

Summary

On multilingual sites, AI Context no longer sends an unpublished translation (Draft or Archived) of a context item to AI prompts or tool output. The published default-language text is used instead, and the item is left out when that is not published either. This applies to every user, including administrators. Non-admin users also now get a published translation of a draft source item, and context push no longer fails for them when a selected item has an unpublished translation in the request language. Sites with moderated translations, where translations often start as Draft, were most exposed.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

Status is stored per translation, but AiContextLanguageService::translateItem() returned a requested translation whenever it existed. The List, Load and selector paths checked access('view') on the default translation before the language switch. As a result, an Archived translation could be shown to a user who only had the published-context permission. A draft source with a published translation was dropped. The selector threw an AccessException. The parent text sent in the conditional subcontext prompt used the translated parent, so it was exposed too.

translateItem() now works from getUntranslated(). It returns the requested translation only if isPublished(), and otherwise returns the default translation. translateItems() now filters. It keeps an item only if the chosen translation is published and access('view') passes on that translation. isPublished() is checked first on purpose, because the boolean access() call drops cacheability. That is safe only for published translations, since the per-user owner access result applies to unpublished ones.

The per-item access('view') loops on the default translation were removed from AiContextSelector (loadPublishedItemsByIds() and the chunk loader), ListAiContextItems and LoadAiContextItemById, because all delivery paths already call translateItems(). List and Load now return No context items are available. and None of the requested context items are available. when nothing survives. Subcontext children passed through translateItems() are also dropped when their delivered translation is unpublished or not viewable. The issue says a follow-up, #3586617, replaces this boolean check for children with one that keeps access cacheability. Docs under docs/ were updated, and new kernel tests cover the reader, admin, conditional-prompt and EchoAI agent cases.

item.title: #3589001: Accessibility skills misstate how #states hides fields, table scope and #type item_list
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +45/−34 · md +43/−32 · yml +1/−1 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 3e3e9af
  • Discussion: #3589001 · 1 contributor · 9 comments

Summary

The accessibility skills in AI Best Practices contained three claims that don't match Drupal core, and they are now corrected. #states is client-side only, which is the real reason to use #access for permission-based hiding. #type => 'table' does not add scope attributes by itself. item_list is a theme hook, so lists need #theme => 'item_list', because #type => 'item_list' renders nothing. The recommended practices stay the same. Only the stated reasons and the example code changed.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The edits are in the drupal-accessibility dispatcher SKILL.md, drupal-a11y-fapi (including its SYNC.md), drupal-a11y-dom, and the fapi evals.

#states: the old text said it leaves hidden fields in the accessibility tree. The issue points out that the state:visible handler in core/misc/states.js toggles the field's wrapper with jQuery, which sets display: none, so the element does leave the accessibility tree. The text now says #states acts only in the browser. item.title: #3586593: Entity Types scope loads the request entity without a view access check
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI

  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 15 files, +1422/−41 · php +1343/−26 · md +78/−15 · yml +1
  • Diff: 671cae1
  • Discussion: #3586593 · 1 contributor · 41 comments

Summary

The Entity Types scope no longer reveals whether a hidden entity exists or which bundle it belongs to. Before, a user with the access published ai context permission could pass an entity type and ID to an agent tool or AI request and see whether a bundle-scoped context item was selected. That worked even for an unpublished node or term they could not view. Now an entity the user cannot view is treated like an ID that does not exist. There is a side effect to check on your site. Editors who can edit an entity but not view it (for example, another author's draft) no longer get Entity Types or Taxonomy Terms matching on that form. Background runs as Anonymous (cron, queues, Drush) also lose bundle-scoped items unless that account can view the entity. A bundle hint sent for an unsaved entity, such as a node add form, still works.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Minor information disclosure: a user with access published ai context could learn whether an entity ID exists and its bundle through the Entity Types scope. Existence and bundle only, no field data.

Technical details

AiContextRequestInfoResolver::getEntityTypeFromEntity() used to load the request entity by ID with no access check. It now calls loadContentEntity(), which already checked access('view'), and returns NULL when the entity is missing or not viewable. The getEntityType() fallback to the caller-supplied bundle hint is unchanged. The resolver now keeps the access result (getContentEntityAccessResult(), allowed or denied). It runs on the revision or translation the route upcasts, not the default revision.

AiContextSelector adds that access result's cacheability to every selection result, including a denied one. This applies even when the Entity Types and Taxonomy Terms scopes are disabled, so a custom scope cannot reuse another account's result. When access depends on ownership (for example, View own unpublished content), the result varies by user.

Because access now decides the match, the resolver takes @current_user as a new constructor argument. The ai_context.request_info_resolver service definition is updated, and any code that instantiates the final class directly must pass an AccountInterface as the fifth argument. The entity and getEntityType() memos reset when the current request (held as a WeakReference) or the account ID changes. An account switch in a queue worker or a nested request therefore re-checks access. applyRequestInfo() also clears a route entity saved for an earlier request, so a later caller-supplied entity is applied. Without that, the earlier route entity would hide it. The docs and a new kernel test class, AiContextEntityBundleAccessTest, cover these cases. Existing Entity Types tests now set up a current user with access content.

Upgrade

If you construct AiContextRequestInfoResolver yourself, for example in tests, pass the current user as the new last argument:

new AiContextRequestInfoResolver(
  $routeMatch,
  $requestStack,
  $entityTypeManager,
  $entityTypeBundleInfo,
  $container->get('current_user'),
);

If editors rely on Entity Types or Taxonomy Terms matching on edit forms, make sure their role can view the content it edits.

item.title: #3586551: Keep consumer overrides during any module uninstall, including automators on automator chain fields
item.description:

  • Diff: d3f7d5a
  • Discussion: #3586551 · 1 contributor · 44 comments

Summary

Saved per-consumer context overrides (ai_context.consumers rows for agents and automators) are now kept whenever a module is uninstalled. Before, some overrides were silently lost while their siblings survived. This happened when several modules were uninstalled in one run with a cross-module dependency, and when an automator was attached to a field on an automator_chain bundle and ai_automators was uninstalled. Kept rows show in the consumers listing as Off (type unavailable), or Off (stale) if the consumer type is still installed (for example when only a module an automator depends on is uninstalled). An admin can remove them with Remove configuration. Reinstalling a module that recreates the host entity with the same ID makes the saved override apply again. Deleting a single agent or automator while its module stays installed still removes its row immediately.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New @internal service ai_context.removed_consumer_rows (tagged persist); AiContextScopeCleanupService gains restoreRemovedConsumerRows().

Technical details

The earlier approach kept a drupal_static list filled by hook_module_preuninstall() and compared it with the deleted entity's type provider. It missed cases where the provider differs from the module being uninstalled, or where the delete happens before the module is listed. Core deletes host entities at two points. ConfigManager::uninstall() flags config entities with isUninstalling(). Before that, ModuleInstaller::uninstall() deletes bundles, and the resulting FieldConfig dependents are deleted with a plain delete() and no flag.

ai_context_entity_delete() now returns early when the host is a ConfigEntityInterface with isUninstalling() TRUE. For all other host deletes the row is removed as before, but AiContextScopeCleanupService::removeDeletedConsumerConfig() first records it in AiContextRemovedConsumerRows. That service is @internal, tagged persist so it survives container rebuilds during an uninstall, and has no constructor dependencies, since a persisted instance would keep the old container's services. It keeps only the first row per consumer ID, matching how duplicate IDs resolve elsewhere.

ai_context_modules_uninstalled() calls restoreRemovedConsumerRows(), which appends recorded rows to ai_context.consumers unless a row with that ID is already present, and clears the list. It runs before the stale-scope scrub so restored rows are scrubbed too. It also runs during config sync, where only the scrub is skipped. It does nothing when ai_context itself is uninstalled. ai_context_module_preuninstall() and ai_context_uninstalling_modules() are removed. Accepted edge case: a row removed earlier in the same request, before an uninstall, is also restored. docs/developers/hooks.md and consumer_api.md are updated, and consumer_api.md now defines "host entity". Kernel tests and a new ai_context_test_automator_dependent test module cover the cases.

Upgrade

Code that implemented or documented reliance on hook_module_preuninstall() or ai_context_uninstalling_modules() from this module should drop it. Both are removed, and ai_context_uninstalling_modules() was @internal.

item.description:

The corrected pass rate on a result page now appears only when the judge was validated at the same question pass threshold the run used. Before, a judge validated at 3.0 could correct a run scored at 3.5 with no warning, which gave a number nobody had measured. When the thresholds differ, or the result did not record its threshold, the Corrected Pass Rate row reads "Not available" with both thresholds, and the EEE export leaves the corrected value out. The fix is to validate the judge again at the threshold the run used. Existing results can change to Not available after the update. A validation where the judge only ever scored 0 or 5 is exempt, since every threshold in between gives the same verdict. Older validations need a rerun to record that evidence. The same commit also ships several related judge-trust fixes (#3594812, #3594813, #3594815, #3594816, #3594817).

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Database update: ai_eval_update_10050 adds nullable endpoint_only, not_scored, pass_items and fail_items columns to ai_eval_judge_validation.
  • Config change: Question pass thresholds (site settings, target form, guided test form) now accept at most two decimals; the number step changed from 0.1 to 0.01.
  • API change: CorrectedPassRateInterface::forResult() and bootstrapForResult() take an optional $runThreshold; omitting it returns NULL (no correction). New thresholdMismatch() method on CorrectedPassRateInterface and JudgeGateTrustInterface, so custom implementations and mocks must add it.

CorrectedPassRate::forResult() and bootstrapForResult() now require a recorded $runThreshold and a compatible validation threshold. The compatibility check is ScoreScale::thresholdMismatch(). Thresholds match when they agree at two decimals, and a positive threshold that rounds to zero never matches zero. Otherwise, a validation flagged endpoint_only fits any run threshold above 0 and up to 5. The evidence is measured from the scores (new endpoint_only column), not inferred from a judge's name or declared range. Legacy rows have NULL there, so they get no exemption.

A new thresholdMismatch() method on CorrectedPassRate returns the two thresholds for an otherwise eligible judge. EvalResultsController reads the run threshold from question_pass_threshold in the dataset snapshot. When no correction is produced, it renders the "Not available" message, with a separate wording when the run recorded no threshold.

To make "same threshold" mean the same thing in both places, validation and run scoring now share ScoreScale::passes(), which compares the score rounded to two decimals. LabeledExample::graderPassesAt() and the result page's low-score check both use it. Before, a score of 3.496 at threshold 3.5 failed validation but passed a run. The threshold inputs on the settings, target and guided test forms now use step 0.01 and reject more than two decimals. The validation controller applies the same rule. Docs in scoring.md, judges.md and the EEE export docs, plus the CHANGELOG, were updated.

Summary

Trace import in ai_eval now handles the structured JSON that ai_observability writes by default. Before, a structured span showed up in trace review as one user message full of raw JSON, and tool calls were lost. Messages now appear as separate messages, tool calls show on the review card, and the reply is the reply text. Spans that ai_observability cut or summarized are flagged and cannot be promoted, and neither can traces with tool calls or tool results in their input, because replay cannot send those yet. The importer also no longer drops every document after a stray closing brace in a trace file. It reports how many parts were skipped, and warns when the rest of a file was not read because of an unclosed brace. The warnings appear on the import page and in drush ai-eval:import-traces. Plain role-line input is read more reliably too: text before the first role line is kept, Windows line endings work, and developer is shown as system.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New Drupal\ai_eval\Service\TracePayloadParser with parseInput(), parseOutput(), parsePlain() and hasCutSignature(), and TraceImporter::splitDocumentsWithReport().

Technical details

The new TracePayloadParser replaces OtelTraceSource::parseMessages(). parseInput() treats input starting with {"messages":[ as structured. It keeps each message's role and text, each assistant message's tool calls (id, name, arguments as a string) and each tool message's tool_id. Anything else goes through parsePlain(). parseOutput() uses normalized.text and normalized.tools when the output is a chat normalized object. Other outputs, such as embeddings, are returned unchanged.

Cut detection does not depend on the 1024 default. hasCutSignature() looks for the [...] marker at the midpoint position where ai_observability's truncation puts it, for strings of at least 32 characters. When a payload is cut, only complete leading message objects from the retained head are recovered. Flags (input_cap, output_cap, omitted, shortened) land in payload_flags on the normalized trace, set truncated, and drive the review card notices. OtlpSpanMapper also uses these checks when setting the stored truncated column. Normalized traces gain raw_input, input_format, response_tools, response_incomplete and payload_flags.

PromotionService has a new STATUS_TOOL_TURNS (tool_turns) refusal. It applies to structured input containing tool role messages, tool calls or call ids. Promoted questions now store metadata.raw_input (up to 8000 characters) and, for tool-only replies, metadata.ai_response_tools as a JSON string. Both are strings so questions stay editable. The streamed_uncaptured check no longer fires when the reply has tool calls or was cut.

On the document side, TraceImporter::splitDocumentsWithReport() scans depth-zero objects with a string-aware matcher. Stray text, stray } and closed non-OTLP objects are skipped and logged with a byte offset. An unclosed object or string stops the read, since later objects could be nested payload data. ImportResult gains skippedDocuments and unreadTails. splitDocuments() still exists and delegates to the new method.

Upgrade

Spans already imported keep their stored truncated value, so re-import them to get the new cut and summarized flags. Parsing of messages and replies happens when a trace is read. Observed tool calls do not fill Expected tools during promotion.
